This VCF contains no homozygous-reference genotypes at any of PharmCAT's required positions, which means it is almost certainly a variants-only file. Such a file is indistinguishable from one where those positions were never tested. For a genotype caller that reads a missing position as reference, the consequence is NOT a missing result — it is a confident WRONG result: a change whose key position is missing is invisible, so a reduced-function patient is reported as normal. Measured rate of confidently-wrong calls at 60% position coverage: up to 28.6%. This application therefore reports genes without their required positions as Unknown rather than as normal. Produce the file again with EVERY position reported — including the ones that match the reference — so each required position carries an explicit genotype. The input requirements page gives the exact commands. See docs/input_requirements.md.

Every gene (9 of 9) was declined, at 0–11% position coverage. That pattern is a property of the FILE, not of 9 separate genes — and it has two common causes.

This looks like a research-format or SNP-array export.

• A research VCF (1000 Genomes, gnomAD, most sequencing pipelines) is POLYMORPHIC-FILTERED: it lists only positions where someone differed from the reference. The positions that matched are simply absent, and absent is indistinguishable from never-tested.
• A consumer export (23andMe, AncestryDNA) is a GENOTYPING ARRAY, not sequencing. It reports a few hundred thousand chosen positions across the whole genome, which is not the same as reporting every position one gene needs.
